items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I presented the pianist as Barney, the saxophonist as Mike... I rehearsed with the musicians... Mike, who played alto sax, was Michel de Villers.

ctx.x: After having a meal in a restaurant near the Opera, a place that I was very familiar with, Serge took me to the theatre where the concert was to take place. It was not far from the Opera either, and I found out the name of the theatre was Edouard the 7th. The musicians I was to do the concert with were there, and I was presented to them. A couple of them spoke english, and that was a big help to me because the few words I had known in French, I had forgotten them all, except 'Yes'(in French, 'oui').

But what surprised me most of all was that these fellows were all young and not one was over 30 and they knew most of all the jazz standards and classics' that I knew and some modern ones that I didn't know. So there was no sweat getting a programme together. But I could not remember the musicians' names, so when we were doing the concert to a full house, I presented the pianist as Barney, the saxophonist as Mike, the vibraphone player was Joe, the bass player John, and the drummer - Rodger. Another surprise was…

And I was also surprised at the large following that jazz had as compared to the public that afternoon in the theatre. I suppose I was better known to the jazz public here than I realized I was, because I had never had such a warm and enthusiastic reception. I was happy about the way the musicians had supported me, and after the concert, my old friend Maurice Cullaz and his wife Yvonette, whom I had known very well since 1935, came backstage to greet me. I was surprised to see the wife of Frans Jackson whose name…
